newsitem.title: ITALY: German EMU delay bid "possible" - Italy's Prodi.
newsitem.headline: German EMU delay bid "possible" - Italy's Prodi.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said in a television interview on Friday that he thought it was "possible" that Germany would ask for a delay to the start of Europe's planned single currency in 1999.

"That is their business. It is also possible," Prodi said in response to a question in the interview, recorded for broadcast by Italian RAI television later on Friday. He said Italy itself would not request a delay. "We must be ready," Prodi said.

Talk of delay to the single currency has become rife in unofficial circles. One element behind the talk has been that Germany and France need to find a way to keep Italy's weaker economy out of the first wave of countries to adopt the new currency.
Another element has been than Germany's unemployment queues will stifle Bonn's ability to cut the country's deficit to qualify for economic and monetary union.
Prodi was asked if he thought Germany, rather than Italy, could seek a delay. "That is their business. It is also possible. We must be ready...We cannot allow ourselves to ask for a delay," he said.
He also said a request for a delay would not be easy for Germany because Chancellor Helmut Kohl had staked his political life on pushing forward with European integration.
